messages:
mike (platform): heads-up — saw a weird canary vs baseline on the rollout dashboard for routing-v2. 95p latency jumps ~40% for a tiny traffic slice (2%). wondering if this is noise or a genuine regress. can we get a quick drilldown and an explainability trace? :thinking:

anya (product): ugh, thanks for flagging. do we have the traffic-split attribution on that view? i want to see which tenant buckets hit the new variant. could be a single noisy client.

ito (eng-platform): pinging @liz for attribution. if we can map request attributes -> model variant + region, we can slice. should be doable with the telemetry index.

liz (dataeng): i can pull the slice. quick note: our current canary dashboard shows aggregate deltas but not the composed signal (latency vs error vs payload-size). might need a short query to isolate 95p latencies by tenant. will run now.

sre-bot: deploy 2026-06-03T09:02:12Z routed 2.1% traffic to routing-v2 (canary). canary-id=canary-20260603-9

mike (platform): thanks bot. if this is tenant-specific, we should consider automated rollback conditions: e.g., if >25% regression on critical tenants OR >30% regress overall for 5m. debating whether to tie that into the rollout guards or keep it as alert-only. thoughts?

ito (eng-platform): i'd prefer a guard hook. alerts are noisy — they tell us after the fact. guard should evaluate composite signals and short-circuit traffic. but we need explainability so the on-call can see "why" it tripped.

chloe (design): from UX POV, show the top three contributing slices when guard fires (tenant, route, seq-length). keep the CTA: "rollback" and "open RCA". no more than 2 clicks.

liz (dataeng): ran the query. partial results:

```
select tenant, count(*) as qps, percentile(latency_ms, 95) as p95
from telemetry_inference
where canary_id = 'canary-20260603-9' and ts >= now() - interval '10 minutes'
group by tenant
order by p95 desc
limit 20;
```

tenant-foo shows p95=420ms vs baseline 290ms, qps=4rps. tenant-bar is fine. looks like tenant-foo dominates the delta.

mike (platform): interesting — tenant-foo has large batched requests sometimes, could blow up p95. can we check payload size / batch-size?

liz (dataeng): yes, another slice: payload_size and seq_len show tenant-foo has a heavy tail. median payload_size 2.3MB, seq_len median 1024. that explains some latency. but still curious why baseline didn't see it. maybe routing-v2 changed streaming/chunking behavior.

ito (eng-platform): that rings true — routing-v2 has different chunk-windowing to optimize throughput; might hurt very large sequences. we should surface that dimension in the canary compare UI. right now it only shows p50/p95/err-rate. add a "slice by payload/seq" button.

anya (product): +1. Also, could we show a small causal explanation: "latency regression concentrated in tenants with high seq_len; likely chunking mismatch" — autogenerated hint to help on-call decide.

mike (platform): for the guard logic: propose two tiers — automatic short-circuit (kill canary) on severe multi-tenant regressions (e.g., >30% p95 reg affecting >3 tenants) and soft alerts for single-tenant regressions with suggested mitigations. we need to document policy plumbed into the rollout API.

ito (eng-platform): agree. API-wise we already accept a "guardPolicy" json in the rollout request. current schema is minimal. maybe extend with: "explainabilityKeys": ["tenant","payload_size","seq_len"], "autoAction": "rollback|pause|notify", and "compositeThresholds" block.

mike (platform): prototype snippet for policy we could support:

```
{
  "guardPolicy": {
    "compositeThresholds": {
      "p95_regression_pct": 30,
      "min_affected_buckets": 3,
      "window_secs": 300
    },
    "explainabilityKeys": ["tenant","seq_len_bucket","route"],
    "autoAction": "rollback",
    "notify": ["oncall@redwood.com"]
  }
}
```

ito (eng-platform): that looks good. implementation note: explainabilityKeys needs a mapping to indexed telemetry fields to compute attribution in <10s. otherwise the guard will be too slow. we'll need a precomputed sketch or summary for recent windows.

liz (dataeng): we can add a rolling OLAP aggregate per minute for those keys. cheap storage. then attribution query is fast. one caveat: cardinality explosion for free-form tenant tags — but tenants are limited to ~500, acceptable.

chloe (design): UI: when guard trips, show the composite card with top-3 contributors and a small sparkline of timeline. allow "open timeline" -> trace view. keep rollback prominent but require a confirmation explaining impact.

anya (product): also add a small "why not rollback automatically" checkbox for teams that want manual control. many customers prefer to be paged instead of auto-rollback.

mike (platform): good point. default to auto-rollback for infra/sre-managed canaries, and default to notify for customer-managed ones.

ito (eng-platform): next steps: liz to prototype the precomputed aggregations, i'll extend rollout API schema, chloe will mock the guard-fire UX, anya will draft product policy options, mike will own rollouts doc update. can we sync tomorrow 10am?

liz (dataeng): noted. i'll have a sample aggregate table and a perf estimate by EOD.

mike (platform): perfect. thanks team. also adding a follow-up: add a lightweight test harness so we can replay tenant-foo's trace against routing-v2 to validate chunking impact before rolling.

sre-bot: reminder: oncall rotation changes next week — update notify list if needed. :calendar:"
